Chapter One: Introduction
1.1 Research Background
With his distinct personality, remarkable talent, and intricate storyline, Sun Wukong, the legendary protagonist of the beloved Chinese novel Journey to the West, has become a cultural icon in China. Since the creation of Wu Chengen in the Ming Dynasty, Sun Wukong has not only been widely known in China, but also its influence transcends national borders and enjoys worldwide fame. He is smart, brave, witty, and humorous, and he perfectly combines the spirit of bravery, wisdom, loyalty, and rebellion, adding infinite splendor to the journey and symbolizing the national spirit of courage, wisdom, and perseverance.
From traditional literature to contemporary film and television, animation, advertising, brand endorsement, and even network literature and social media, Sun Wukong’ s image has long been widely used in a variety of media. Its diversified presentation not only enriches the cultural connotation, but also becomes a bridge between Chinese culture and world culture. However, with the rise of postmodernism, Sun Wukong’ s image began to experience profound changes. In this context, the portrayal of Sun Wukong shows the characteristics of authoritative resolution and parody collage. Many film and television works deconstruct the structure of the original story and the relationship between characters, integrate the personal perspective of the creator, and create the image of Sun Wukong with their own characteristics.
The contemporary interpretation of Sun Wukong’ s image has been greatly impacted by postmodernism, which is characterized by its artistic style of no depth, no center, no basis, self-reflection, gamification, simulation, eclecticism, and pluralism. In the cross-cultural context, Sun Wukong gradually changes from the traditional hero symbol to a complex and multi-faceted character, which is not only reflected in the external image and personality characteristics, but also goes deeper into the inner world and emotional expression. In modern film and television works, the character of Sun Wukong’ s rebellion has been significantly amplified and even has a “dark” color. For example, in A Chinese Odyssey to the West, he not only challenges the authority of heaven, but also questions his own destiny and existential significance. Such deep rebellion and self-exploration make the image of Sun Wukong more three-dimensional and real and close to the aesthetic needs of modern audiences.
In addition, modern works give Sun Wukong more personal emotions and psychological descriptions; he is no longer a single dimension of the hero but has multiple personalities and complex emotions of the individual. This change is not only a reinterpretation of the traditional hero image but also reflects modern people’s pursuit of individuality and freedom.
1.2 The Importance and Objective of the Study
We can better understand the flexibility and malleability of cultural symbols by examining the postmodernist interpretation of Sun Wukong’ s appearance. As an important symbol of traditional Chinese culture, Sun Wukong’ s image has undergone constant evolution and reconstruction in different historical periods and cultural environments. The postmodern culture, with its characteristics of decentralization, diversification, and fragmentation, provides new possibilities and space for the interpretation of Sun Wukong’ s image. This study helps us better comprehend the complexity and diversity of cultural interactions by illuminating the ways in which cultural symbols acquire new meanings and values in various cultural contexts.
In addition, this research also has important academic value and practical significance. At the academic level, it enriches our understanding and application of postmodern cultural theories and provides a new perspective and method for cross-cultural research. In practice, through the postmodernist interpretation of Sun Wukong’ s image, we can provide beneficial inspiration and reference for the innovation and development of cultural industry. For instance, this research can give us helpful advice on how to better incorporate traditional cultural components with contemporary aesthetic principles and how to develop cultural goods that appeal to people from different cultural backgrounds when making animation, video games, and other media.
Chapter Two: Theoretical Basics
2.1 An Overview of Postmodernism Theory
Postmodernism theory is a complex and diversified trend of thought that originates from modernism but rebels against it. It criticizes and deconstructs the thinking modes of subjectivity, sensory richness, wholeness, centrality, and identity that emerged in the process of modernization and criticizes and deconstructs essentialism, foundationalism, and “presence metaphysics” of traditional Western philosophy.
Postmodernism theory emphasizes the rebellion and innovation of modernism. It refuses to regulate the world with unity and wholeness, opposes explaining the world with fixed logic and rules, respects differences, and advocates the coexistence of diversity. This theory advocates the elimination of depth mode towards the sense of flatness, the elimination of essence with phenomenon, the elimination of center with edge, and the elimination of reality with fiction (text). It is opposed to individualism and pays more attention to the relationship between individuals and society and how people should better adapt to the information and commercialization of high-tech society (Lele Qu 2024). However, postmodernism also encourages innovation because it holds that knowledge is socially constructed rather than a reaction to reality. As a result, it encourages people to fully express their creativity, challenge conventional wisdom, and look for a fresh and worthwhile perspective.
In terms of values, postmodernism shows a pluralistic form, emphasizing uncertainty, intertextuality, and intersubjectivity. Rewrite these sentences: I didn’ t understand the means. This relativist attitude reflects the recognition of uncertainty in history and the development of things and does not believe that there is an essential, universal, absolute truth.
In addition, the theory of postmodernism also involves the criticism of modern society. It condemns the failure of modern society to live up to its various promises and rejects such things as worldviews, wholeness, and movement and attitudes towards life as central to social development. At the same time, it gives greater importance to pre-modern phenomena such as emotion, intuition, experience, myth, and so on, rejecting the boundaries that modern society places between disciplines, between culture and life, between fiction and theory, and between imagination and reality.
2.2 Intercultural Image Interpretation
Image interpretation in a cross-cultural context is a complex and multi-dimensional process, which involves the interweaving and collision of different cultural backgrounds, values, cognitive modes, and historical experiences. In this process, images or symbols in one culture are reinterpreted and given new meanings in the context of another culture, which may even lead to misunderstandings and conflicts between cultures, but may also promote cultural exchange and integration.
Image interpretation in a cross-cultural context requires a high degree of cultural sensitivity and openness (Liang Jingyu 2023:665-686). This implies that when interpreting, we should respect and recognize the distinctiveness of other cultures and refrain from imposing our own cultural viewpoints on others. To expand our own cultural perspective, we need to simultaneously maintain an open mind and be prepared to accept and value new aspects and variability in other cultures.
The image interpretation in the cross-cultural context requires the use of interdisciplinary perspectives and methods. Since images often carry rich cultural connotations and symbolic meanings, it is necessary to comprehensively apply the knowledge and theories of literature, art, history, sociology, psychology, and other disciplines in the interpretation. In this way, we can not only dig deeper into the cultural implication behind the image, but also more comprehensively understand the transmission and acceptance process of the image in different cultural contexts.
In addition, the image interpretation in the cross-cultural context also needs to pay attention to the differences and commonalities between cultures. Different cultures have differences in values, ways of thinking, habits of behavior, etc. These differences may lead to different interpretations of the same image. However, there are also commonalities between cultures, such as the longing for a better life and the pursuit of truth, kindness, and beauty. In the process of interpretation, these commonalities should be keenly captured in order to promote mutual understanding and respect between cultures.
The process of interpreting images in a cross-cultural setting is dynamic. With the in-depth development of globalization, the communication and integration between different cultures are becoming more and more frequent, and the interpretation of images in different cultural contexts is constantly changing. As a result, in order to adjust to the evolving requirements of picture interpretation in a cross-cultural setting, we should always be aware of cultural dynamics and update our knowledge and notions.
2.3 An Overview of the Image of Sun Wukong
Sun Wukong is the core character in Journey to the West. His image is deeply rooted in people’s hearts and has a high degree of recognition and rich connotation. He is a stone monkey, born in Huaguo Mountain, born with divine power, brave, and fearless. In the process of growing up, he crossed the sea to learn art, diligent and studious, and eventually practiced 72 kinds of change, somersault cloud, and other superb skills, and he has a fire eye and can see through the evil tricks.
The character of Sun Wukong is distinct and complex. He was brave and decisive, not afraid of power, and dared to challenge authority, and the uproar in Heaven Palace was the concentrated embodiment of his spirit of resistance. At the same time, he was jealous of evil, good and evil clearly, loyal to Master Tang Monk, cared for his younger brothers, and did away with evil demons. In addition, he also has smart, hardworking, humiliation-bearing, determined, and other excellent qualities. In the process of going west, he volunteered, charged in front, fought with the evil forces at the forefront, and made great contributions to the success of the scripture team (Mengqingjuan & Wangjing 2024).
The image of Sun Wukong is also full of contradictions and complexities. He is not only a rebel, but also a responsible hero. He acted in ways that were often outside the bounds of convention and morality, but he always held fast to his inner beliefs and principles. This contradiction and complexity make his image more three-dimensional, full, and attractive.
The image of Sun Wukong also has significant vitality and influence in the cross-cultural setting. He is not only an important symbol of Chinese traditional culture, but also a treasure in the treasure house of world culture. His stories have been translated into many languages and spread across the globe, becoming a bridge and bond connecting different cultures and countries.
Chapter Three: The Historical Evolution and Cultural Significance of Sun Wukong’ s Image
3.1 The Image of Sun Wukong’ s Origin and Prototype
It took a long time for Sun Wukong, a mythical character from the Chinese epic Journey to the West, to develop and become infused with many cultural components. Before Journey to the West was written, mythological characters similar to the Monkey King had been documented. In the Northern Song Dynasty, the Dunhuang murals in the Western Xia Dynasty depicted the image of a monkey following Xuanzang’ s pilgrimage. In the Southern Song Dynasty (also believed to be the Yuan Dynasty), there appeared a book about Tang Monk’ s Sutras. In it, there appeared a character named “Monkey Walker.” This monkey walker not only had strong magic power, but also took on the responsibility of protecting Tang Monk’ s Sutras, which were considered to be one of the important sources of Sun Wukong’ s image.
About the prototype of Sun Wukong, there has been a wide discussion and speculation in the academic circles and among the people. One view is that the Monkey King is based on the golden monkey from the Sichuan and Yunnan provinces of China, which is famous for its golden hair, heart-shaped face, and lively and cute personality, and has certain similarities with the image of Sun Wukong. Though intuitive, this assertion is not backed up by concrete data. According to another theory, the Monkey King might have been inspired by the water monster “Wu Zhiqi” of the Huai River. Wu Zhiqi is often recorded in ancient literature, and its image is “like an ape, golden eyes and snow teeth, light and swift,” which is similar to the monkey image and the fiery eyes of Sun Wukong. At the same time, Wu Zhi Qi had also stirred up trouble, obstructing the Great Yu to control the water, and then was captured and suppressed by the Great Yu, which is similar to the experience of Sun Wukong after the uproar in Heaven was suppressed by the Tathagata Buddha at the foot of the Five Elements. Mr. Lu Xun also put forward a similar view in his academic work History of Chinese Novels (Nicolle Zimmermann et al.,2024).
Furthermore, some people believe that Sun Wukong is modeled after the Indian epic Ramayana’s Hanuman, the monkey deity. Hanuman went through hardships to help Rama save his wife, and Sun Wukong went through ninety-nine eighty-one difficulties to help the Tang monk. At the same time, Hanuman is the grand general of the Monkey Kingdom, and Sun Wukong is the Monkey King and the Great Sage of the Sky, both of which are similar in identity and heroic deeds. Hu Shi also put forward the view that the image of Sun Wukong comes from Hanuman in his Research on Journey to the West.
In fact, the figure of Sun Wukong probably incorporates a variety of elements and cultural backgrounds, including local Chinese myths and legends, similar characters from foreign cultures, and interpretations of folklore by artists and storytellers. These elements together constitute the cultural origin and multiple sources of the classic image of Sun Wukong.
3.2 Developing the Persona of Sun Wukong in Journey to the West
Sun Wukong is a human, monkey, and divine figure in Journey to the West. He looks like a monkey with agile, lively, and active movements, retaining much of the nature of the monkey. At the same time, he has human wisdom and emotion, can think independently, is full of justice, is loyal to Master Tang Monk, and cares for his younger brothers Zhu Bajie and Sha Seng. In addition, he also has a divine nature, with 72 kinds of changes, somersault clouds, and other magical abilities, and can overcome various demons and ghosts to protect the safety of the scripture team.
In shaping the image of Sun Wukong, the author Wu Chengen skillfully uses a series of plots and details to show his character and spiritual style. Through the story of Sun Wukong, he shows his rebellious spirit of resisting authority and pursuing freedom; through Sun Wukong’ s protection of Tang Monk’ s journey to the west, he shows his loyalty, bravery, and heroic spirit. Through Sun Wukong’ s struggle with all kinds of demons and ghosts, he shows his resourcefulness, flexibility, and wisdom (Weichi Shi 2024).
The author's desire for independence, defiance of persecution, and search for the truth are also reflected in the picture of Sun Wukong. He is not bound by heaven, not limited by the teachings of Buddhism, dares to challenge authority, and pursues individuality and freedom. This spirit had a positive significance in the social background at that time, reflecting people’ s dissatisfaction with the feudal autocratic rule and their desire for individual liberation.
In addition, the image of Sun Wukong also contains rich cultural connotations. He is not only an important role in ancient Chinese myths and legends, but also a symbol of wisdom and power in traditional Chinese culture. His image not only represents the ancient people’ s worship of heroes and wisdom, but also reflects the ancient people’s pursuit of justice and truth.
3.3 Development and Propagation of Sun Wukong’ s Image in Various Cultural Contexts
The dissemination and evolution of the image of Sun Wukong in different cultural contexts is a complicated and interesting process, which not only reflects the changes of Chinese culture in different historical periods, but also reflects the exchange and integration of different cultures.
The character of Sun Wukong first appeared in literature and folklore in ancient China. Before Journey to the West was written, mythological characters similar to the Monkey King had been documented. With the wide spread of Journey to the West, the image of Sun Wukong has gradually penetrated into people’ s hearts, and he has become a mythical hero with a distinct personality and extraordinary ability. He is witty, brave, and rebellious, possessed of 72 magic spells and a golden staff, all of which make Sun Wukong one of the most charming characters in traditional Chinese literature.
Into the modern era, the image of Sun Wukong began to cross the national border and go to the world. In the western perspective, the image of Sun Wukong is not unchanged but gradually evolves with the spread and interpretation of culture. In the early English and American missionary translations, Sun Wukong was only a supporting role, but with the development of German Sinology, Sun Wukong gradually became the leading role. This change not only reflects the Western understanding and construction path of Chinese culture, but also reflects the complex relationship between Eastern and Western cultures in the collision and mutual learning.
In Western culture, the image of Sun Wukong is endowed with more divine and heroic qualities. For example, the German Sinologist Willey-Hsien compiled Chinese Folk Tales with Sun Wukong as the main character, significantly elevating his status in Western culture (Bizhanhe 2023). At the same time, the depiction of Sun Wukong by western artists is also different; some highlight his animal nature, and some give him heroic characteristics, which further enriches the image of Sun Wukong in Western culture.
With the in-depth development of globalization, Sun Wukong’ s image has further crossed the dimensional wall and is active in emerging cultural fields such as animation and games. In these fields, the image of Sun Wukong has been given more modern and innovative elements, and has become a more diversified and three-dimensional cultural symbol. For example, in the "Dragon Ball" series, Monkey King is set as a super soldier with Saiyan blood, and his passionate battle scenes and warm and moving friendship stories have sparked a global craze.
The way that Sun Wukong’ s image spreads and changes across cultural contexts is a dynamic process. It not only reflects the changes and development of Chinese culture in different historical periods but also reflects the exchange and integration of different cultures. In this process, the image of Sun Wukong has been continuously endowed with new connotations and meanings, and has become a cultural symbol that crosses national boundaries and times.
3.4 The Cultural Significance and Value of Sun Wukong’ s Image
Sun Wukong is a symbol of humanity’ s unwavering quest for knowledge and independence. Since he was born, he has been unwilling to be bound by any constraints, boldly breaking into the dragon palace and making trouble in the underworld, showing his resistance to established rules and his insistence on free will. This desire for freedom reflects the deep human instinct for freedom and self-actualization. At the same time, he is clever and witty, with the wisdom and courage to overcome one difficulty after another, becoming the embodiment of wisdom and power.
The growth course of Sun Wukong also contains profound cultural connotations of self-transcendence and practice. From the initial ignorance and willfulness to the later suffering on the way to the sutras, he gradually became mature, stable, and responsible and completed the transformation from “demon” to “Buddha.” This process symbolizes the process of constantly overcoming one’s own shortcomings and improving oneself on the road of life. It teaches us to have the courage to face our own shortcomings, through continuous learning and sharpening, to achieve spiritual sublimation and personality improvement (Chenhoujun 2023).
Furthermore, Sun Wukong is a symbol of courage and righteousness. On the way, he brought down demons and protected the four Tang monks, masters and apprentices to overcome numerous obstacles. In the face of powerful monsters, he never flinches, always stands up, and conquers evil with fearless courage and superb skill. This quality of justice and courage has become the spiritual force that inspires people to stick to the right path and go forward in the face of difficulties and injustice.
From the perspective of cultural value, the image of Sun Wukong has been deeply integrated into the cultural gene of the Chinese nation. He became a symbol of courage, wisdom, justice, and freedom, influencing generations of Chinese people. His story is not only widely circulated in China, but also attracted attention around the world, playing an important role in spreading Chinese culture (Fengjing 2024).
In contemporary society, the cultural connotation and value of Sun Wukong still have important enlightenment significance. His quest for freedom reminds us to value our freedoms and defend our rights; his spirit of self-transcendence inspires us to continue to forge ahead and surpass ourselves; and his righteous and courageous qualities inspire us to stand up and stick to the moral bottom line in the face of evil and difficulties.
Chapter Four: Cross-Cultural Postmodernist Interpretation of Sun Wukong’ s Image
4.1 Deconstructing Sun Wukong’ s Image from a Postmodernist Perspective
Postmodernist works often subvert and reshape the image of classic literature by dispelling authority, reconstructing stories, and emphasizing individual feelings. In the image of Sun Wukong, this deconstruction is particularly obvious.
In “A Chinese Odyssey to the West,” the deity of Sun Wukong (the Supreme Treasure) is greatly dissolved, replaced by a more distinct human nature and demon. For example, the Supreme Treasure shows strong personal feelings and desires when faced with the choice between love and a learning mission. He said, “Once true love was placed in front of me, I did not cherish it, and when I lost it, I regretted it too much. The most painful thing in the world is this” (Fanrong 2024). This passage deeply reveals the emotional struggle and desire for love in the heart of the Supreme Treasure, in sharp contrast to the divine image of Sun Wukong in the original book.
Postmodernist works also deconstruct the image of Sun Wukong by subverting the traditional mentoring relationship. In A Chinese Journey to the West, the relationship between Tang Monk and Sun Wukong is no longer the traditional mentoring relationship but becomes more complex and diversified. For example, in order to save Bai Jingjing, the Supreme Treasure repeatedly used the Moon Treasure Box to travel through time and space and even clashed with the Tang monk. During one confrontation, the Supreme Treasure said to the Tang monk, “What’ s the fuss! Do you realize that you have committed a terrible crime? Do you realize how many innocent people you have killed?” (Kongdegang 2023) This passage not only reflects Zhunbao’ s boredom and dissatisfaction with Tang Monk, but also implies the subversion and reconstruction of the mentoring relationship.
The image of Sun Wukong is also deconstructed in postmodernist works through collage and the displacement of time and space. In “A Chinese Odyssey to the West,” the confusion and collage of time and space make Sun Wukong’ s story more complex and diversified. For example, in the process of traveling through time and space, the Supreme Treasure encounters himself and other characters at different points in time, and the dialogue and interaction between these characters constitute the unique narrative structure of the film. Among them, the Supreme Treasure’s affectionate confession in the face of Zixia Fairy: “Once there was a sincere love in front of me, I did not cherish...” (Liuliang 2024) This passage not only reflects the Supreme Treasure’s persistence and pursuit of love, but also makes the image of Sun Wukong more three-dimensional and diversified through the confusion and collage of time and space.
The post-modernist interpretation of Sun Wukong’ s image in a cross-cultural setting highlights his humanity and demon while dispelling his divinity. The mentoring relationship is subverted and reconstructed; time and space confusion and collage make Sun Wukong’s story more complex and diversified. These deconstruction techniques not only enrich the image connotation of Sun Wukong, but also provide the audience with more diversified interpretation and imagination space.
4.2 Examining Sun Wukong’ s Image Through a Postmodernist Lens
In the cross-cultural context, the classic literary image of Sun Wukong has undergone many reconstructions, which are not only reflected in the changes of his appearance, character, and story line, but also reflected in the changes of his cultural connotation and symbolic meaning.
In the cross-cultural context, the image of Sun Wukong is first given more modernity and human color. For example, in the American cartoon The Monkey King, Sun Wukong is portrayed as a more humorous, witty, and humanized character. He will not only display his supernatural abilities as in traditional stories, but also share his inner monologues and life philosophies with the audience. For example, when facing difficulties, Sun Wukong might say, “No matter how many difficulties and obstacles lie ahead, I will not give up, because I am me, the unique Sun Wukong!” This kind of humanized treatment makes the image of Sun Wukong closer to the modern audience, and it is easier to arouse the audience’s resonance and love.
In addition, in the cross-cultural context, the image of Sun Wukong has been given more cultural diversity and inclusiveness. For example, in the Japanese manga Dragon Ball, the image of Son Goku (named “Goku” in the work) is reinterpreted as a warrior with super powers who goes through many adventures and challenges with the other characters. In this story, Sun Wukong not only shows his bravery and wisdom, but also builds a deep friendship and team spirit with other characters. This cross-cultural reconstruction not only injected new vitality into the image of Sun Wukong, but also promoted the communication and understanding between different cultures.
In the cross-cultural context, the image reconstruction of Sun Wukong is also reflected in the change of its symbolic meaning. For example, in the video game Black Myth: Wukong, Sun Wukong is portrayed as a flesh-and-blood, emotionally rich character. He must not only face external threats and challenges, but also face his own internal struggles and contradictions. This remodeling makes the image of Sun Wukong more three-dimensional and fuller, and it is easier to trigger players to think about deep issues such as humanity, freedom, and faith. For example, in a game, Sun Wukong might say, “Although I am a demon, I also have a heart for good. I will use my strength to protect all that I hold dear!” (Lizhu&Wangmeiqing 2022) This expression not only shows Sun Wukong’ s bravery and responsibility, but also reflects his kindness and compassion.
The cross-cultural reconstruction of Sun Wukong’ s image is a form of invention and reconsideration of the traditional literary image. These remodelings not only enriched the image and cultural connotation of Sun Wukong, but also promoted the communication and understanding between different cultures. Through these remodelings, we can see a more diversified, three-dimensional, and full image of Sun Wukong. He is not only the embodiment of courage, wisdom, and rebel spirit, but also a symbol of humanity, freedom, and faith.
4.3 A Study of the Postmodernist Elements of Sun Wukong's Image
4.3.1 Anti-heroism
One of Sun Wukong’ s postmodernist characteristics in the cross-cultural setting is his propensity for anti-heroism. This trait has been extensively mirrored and expanded upon in contemporary cultural works, particularly in animation, television, and film.
An iconic figure from Journey to the West, Sun Wukong was once a courageous, clever, and devoted hero with a strong spirit of revolt, which was primarily manifested in the uprising against injustice. Modern paintings, on the other hand, portray an anti-heroic quality by amplifying and even adding extra “dark” colors to this rebellious attitude.
Take the movie “A Chinese Odyssey to the West” as an example; the image of Sun Wukong has been completely interpreted. In this film, Sun Wukong not only fights against the authority of heaven, but also questions his own destiny and the meaning of his existence. He is no longer the single, perfect hero, but an individual with multiple personalities and complex emotions. He faced his own weaknesses and mistakes, and his heart was full of contradictions and struggles. This deep rebellion and self-exploration make the image of Sun Wukong more three-dimensional and real, but also more in line with the aesthetic needs of modern audiences.
In the film, Sun Wukong’ s classic lines are “Once there was a sincere love in front of me, I did not cherish it until the time of loss was too late to regret; the most painful thing in the world is this. If God can give me a chance to do it again, I will say three words to that girl: ‘I love you.’ If I have to put a time limit on this love, I hope it is ten thousand years!” (Maojie 2023) It reflects his inner tenderness and contradiction. This line not only shows Sun Wukong’ s desire and regret for love, but also reflects his helplessness and struggle against his own fate.
In addition, in Monkey King: Monkey King Is Back, Sun Wukong is portrayed as a hero who has experienced a long period of loneliness and pain. He must not only fight in the face of external enemies, but also overcome inner fear and despair. This display of the inner world also makes the image of Sun Wukong richer and more moving, but also allows the audience to better understand and resonate.
4.3.2 Promiscuity
The image of Sun Wukong in modern culture presents a remarkable mix. This hybridity is not only reflected in the multifaceted nature of his character but also in the multiple interpretations and reconstructions of his image. In the original story of Journey to the West, Sun Wukong is a brave, witty, loyal, and rebellious mythological figure. However, in modern postmodernist works, Sun Wukong’ s image has been given more complexity and multifacetedness.
For example, in the movie A Chinese Odyssey to the West, the image of Sun Wukong is completely subverted. He is no longer the all-powerful, honest, and brave “Monkey King” but is portrayed as a selfish, cowardly, and unscrupulous low-level person. This subversive way of shaping breaks the traditional “divine” image of the Monkey King and makes the image of Sun Wukong present a kind of hybrid. He retains the bravery and wit of the original, while adding new character traits such as selfishness and philandering. This kind of hybrid image-shaping way lets the audience see the other side of Sun Wukong and also triggers the audience’s new thinking about the hero image (Sunyike 2022).
In addition, in Monkey King: Monkey King Is Back, the image of Sun Wukong also presents a mix. He is no longer a simple hero, but a hero who has endured a long period of loneliness and suffering. He must not only fight in the face of external enemies, but also overcome inner fear and despair. This display of the inner world makes the image of Sun Wukong richer and more moving. His image is no longer simple, but contains a variety of emotional elements such as bravery, tenacity, loneliness, and pain.
4.3.3 Irony and parody
Sun Wukong is a well-known figure from Journey to the West, and postmodernist works frequently employ his image for satire and parody. This method exposes a number of inconsistencies and issues in contemporary society in addition to shattering the conventional hero image.
For example, in the movie “A Chinese Odyssey to the West,” the image of Sun Wukong is given the color of irony. He was originally a powerful, all-powerful hero, but in the film, he is portrayed as a poor man, powerless to change his fate. This kind of ironic shaping not only allows the audience to see another side of Sun Wukong, but also causes the audience to think about the real society. In the film, Sun Wukong no longer fights bravely against the authority of heaven, but chooses to escape and compromise. This parody of the hero image not only subverts the traditional heroic narrative, but also reveals the helplessness and powerlessness of modern people in the face of authority.
In addition, in the Biography of Wukong, another postmodernist work, Sun Wukong’ s image is also used as a parody. In the film, he is no longer the brave and fearless hero who pursues freedom but a tragic figure who is bound by heaven and cannot escape his fate. His confrontation with heaven is no longer a simple contest between justice and evil but a profound reflection on fate and freedom. In terms of dialogue, Sun Wukong’ s lines are also full of elements of irony and parody. For example, he said, “I want this day, I can no longer hide my eyes; I want this land; I can no longer bury my heart; I want all sentient beings to understand my intention. I want all the Buddhas to disappear!” This line not only expresses Sun Wukong’ s resistance to the authority of heaven, but also reveals his desire for freedom and destiny. However, this resistance and longing is spoken in the context of his inability to escape the shackles of heaven, and is therefore full of irony and parody (Pengshujun 2024).
The irony and parody features of Sun Wukong’ s image in the postmodernism works are embodied in the subversion of the hero image, the revelation of the real society, and the profound thinking of fate and freedom. This feature not only allows the audience to see another side of Sun Wukong, but also causes the audience to reflect deeply on modern society.
4.3.4 Cultural diversity
As a classic cultural symbol, Sun Wukong’ s image not only occupies an important position in Chinese culture, but also has a wide influence on the world. In the context of postmodernism, the image of Sun Wukong has been given more cultural diversity. He is no longer a single and fixed cultural symbol but a multiple image that can cross cultural boundaries and integrate different cultural elements.
For instance, Sun Wukong’ s image demonstrates significant cultural diversity in the television series and movie Journey to the West and its derivative works. He is a hero in traditional Chinese culture, with qualities such as bravery, wisdom, loyalty, and responsibility, but also incorporates elements of the monkey god Hanuman in Indian mythology, such as great strength, wisdom, and supernatural powers. This cross-cultural integration makes the image of Sun Wukong more three-dimensional and diversified.
In terms of specific discourse quotes, Sun Wukong’ s lines in film and television works also reflect the characteristics of cultural diversity. For example, in Journey to the West, Sun Wukong often speaks some philosophical and profound words when facing difficulties. These words not only reflect the wisdom of traditional Chinese culture, but also integrate elements of other cultures. As Sun Wukong often said after defeating the demon, "Where the monster escapes, eat my old Sun a stick!" This sentence not only embodies Sun Wukong’ s bravery and sense of justice, but also incorporates elements of Chinese martial arts and chivalrous culture. At the same time, Sun Wukong often uses philosophical and profound words when communicating with other characters. For example, he says to Tang Monk, “Master, I know that you are dedicated to Buddha, but you can’t be always compassionate, and you should also punish the wicked.” This sentence not only reflects the wisdom and responsibility of Sun Wukong, but also integrates the thought of “compassion, but also distinguish right from wrong” in traditional Chinese culture (Liuliang 2024).
In addition, in various cultural products in modern society, the image of Sun Wukong has also been given more cultural diversity. For example, in animation, games, movies, and other works, the image of Sun Wukong is often reinterpreted and shaped to adapt to different cultural backgrounds and the needs of audiences. These works not only retain Sun Wukong’ s original bravery, wisdom, and other qualities, but also integrate more modern elements and cross-cultural elements, making Sun Wukong’ s image more fashionable and diversified.
Chapter Five: Analysis of Sun Wukong’ s Image through Postmodernist Interpretation
5.1 Sun Wukong’ s Film and Television Appearances
The postmodernist interpretation of Sun Wukong’ s image is especially evident in the television and film works. Through the dialogue examples in different works, we can see the diversification and cultural integration of this image.
In the TV series Journey to the West, Sun Wukong’ s classic line is “The emperor takes turns to do it; next year to my home.” It shows Sun Wukong’ s challenge to authority and pursuit of equality, which echoes postmodernism’s deconstruction of traditional authority.
In the movie Journey to the West, the Monkey King, played by Stephen Chow, has a well-known line: “Once there was a sincere love in front of me, I did not cherish it, and only when I lost it did, I regret it too much. The most painful thing in the world is this” (Xujianhua 2024). This passage pushes the humanization characteristics of Sun Wukong to the extreme and also reflects postmodernism’ s subversion of the traditional narrative.
In the animated movie Monkey King: Monkey King Is Back, Sun Wukong faces a dilemma and says, “I’ m Monkey King; this little thing is nothing!” This sentence not only reflects Sun Wukong’ s indomitable spirit, but also shows the modern interpretation of him as a heroic image, which is in line with the reconstruction of the heroic image in postmodernism.
In the TV series Sun Wukong, Zhang Weijian’ s version of the Monkey King has a line: “I am Sun Wukong, I am invincible!” Although this sentence retains the self-confidence and domineering of Sun Wukong, it also has a joking and exaggerated component, reflecting the deconstruction and reorganization of traditional images by postmodernism.
In the movie Journey to the West, Sun Wukong, played by Huang Bo, says to the Tang monk, “Believe it or not, I can kill you in one second” (Yuzhengyao & Xieyuanyuan 2020). This cold and threatening tone is quite different from the traditional image of Sun Wukong, showing postmodernism’ s reinterpretation and dark treatment of classic characters.
Through the dialogue examples in these films and television works, we can see the diversity and complexity of Sun Wukong’ s image under the postmodernist interpretation. Each work has been innovated and adapted on the basis of the original culture, making the image of Sun Wukong richer and more three-dimensional, while also reflecting the contemporary society’ s reinterpretation of traditional stories and the integration of diverse cultures.
5.2 The Image of Sun Wukong in Network Animation and Literature
In the network literature and animation works, the postmodernist interpretation of Sun Wukong’ s image is also clear, and the dialogue examples in these works show the diversity and cultural innovation of Sun Wukong’ s image.
“I want this day, no longer hide my eyes; I cannot bury my heart in this land; let all these beings understand my will; let all the Buddhas vanish into thin air!” yelled Sun Wukong violently in the online novel “Wukong Biography” as he faced the oppression of heaven. According to postmodernism’ s deconstruction of central authority, Sun Wukong’s vigorous pursuit of free will and rejection of conventional authority are reflected in this paragraph.
In the anime Seven Dragon Ball, Monkey King says to Flisa, “I will never forgive you; you hurt my friend!” Although Sun Goku here retains the fighting spirit, his image has been integrated into the heroic elements of Japanese anime, showing a new image after cultural integration.
In the Chinese cartoon Monkey King: Monkey King is Back, Monkey King says to Jiang Liuer, “If you have any difficulties in the future, call Monkey King, and I will appear.” This sentence not only reflects the heroic plot of Sun Wukong to save the beauty, but also shows his modern image as a guardian, which is a reshaping of the traditional image of Sun Wukong.
In the online novel Fighting God of War, Sun Wukong faces the enemy and says, “I am the King of Heaven; you small characters also dare to be bold in front of me?” This confidence and arrogance, although retaining the character characteristics of the original, but in the environment of online literature, more emphasis on personality and heroism.
In the cartoon “Monkey King: Monkey King is Back,” Sun Wukong said to the goblins, “You demons and ghosts, all listen to me, this world is not a place where you can do wrong!” This sentence embodies Sun Wukong’ s sense of justice and determination to protect the weak, as well as a modern interpretation of the traditional hero image (Yuanxue 2024).
These dialogue examples in network literature and animation show the richness and innovation of Sun Wukong’ s image under the post-modernist interpretation. Through the deconstruction and recombination of traditional images, Sun Wukong’ s images become more diversified and in line with modern aesthetics, reflecting postmodernism’ s re-creation of classical cultural elements and cross-cultural dialogue.
5.3 The Transmission of Sun Wukong's Image in Intercultural Communication
The spread of Sun Wukong’ s image in cross-cultural communication exemplifies postmodernism, particularly the conversation instances in films and television shows with many cultural origins, which demonstrate the image’ s globalization and diversity.
In the Disney animated film Mulan, although it is not directly about the Monkey King’s work, there is a line in the film: Flexible as a monkey. The metaphor here is clearly influenced by the image of Sun Wukong, showing his influence in Western culture.
In the movie Kung Fu Panda, the protagonist panda Po says, “I am a monkey. Monkeys are the most flexible!” The monkey image here is obviously a tribute to Sun Wukong, integrating the characteristics of Sun Wukong into a completely different cultural background, reflecting the image transmission in cross-cultural communication (Yuanxue 2024).
In the Netflix animated series Stranger Things, the character Dustin says, “I need courage like Son Goku” when facing danger. This statement shows that Sun Wukong’ s image has been deeply rooted in people’ s hearts and even had an impact on American pop culture.
In the Japanese anime Seven Dragon Ball, Sun Goku (Sun Goku is called “Sun Goku” in Japanese) often says, “I am Saiya; I will not lose to anyone!” This indomitable spirit echoes the image of Sun Wukong in Journey to the West but finds a new interpretation in Japanese culture (Yancanwei et al.,2022).
In the international version of the film Journey to the West, Sun Wukong’ s line is translated as “I am the great Monkey King, and I will not bow down to any demon!” This way of translation and communication makes the image of Sun Wukong more international, while retaining the original cultural characteristics.
The dissemination of Sun Wukong’ s image in cross-cultural communication is not only a direct translation or copy of the original work, but also a cultural re-creation and integration. Through the dialogue examples in different film and television works, the image of Sun Wukong has crossed the cultural boundary and become a global cultural symbol, which reflects the characteristics of postmodernism’s resolution of tradition and boundary.
Conclusion
The postmodernist interpretation of Sun Wukong’ s image in the cross-cultural context demonstrates cultural plurality, confusion, irony, and parody. These characteristics make the image of Sun Wukong more three-dimensional and richer in the context of postmodernism. In his postmodernism works, Sun Wukong presents the characteristics of anti-heroism, subverts the traditional hero image, shows multiple personalities and complex emotions, and satisfies the aesthetic needs of modern audiences. The hybridity of Sun Wukong is reflected in the multifaceted nature of his character and the multiple interpretations of his images. Sun Wukong, for instance, is subversively shown in A Chinese Odyssey to the West as a self-centered, avaricious, and simple-minded low-level figure, breaking the conventional picture of a “divine” Monkey King. Sun Wukong’ s post-modernism works also have the features of irony and parody. Through the parody of Sun Wukong, the work reveals the contradictions and problems of modern society, such as helplessness and powerlessness in the face of authority. The postmodern interpretation of Sun Wukong’ s image shows the cultural diversity. In the context of globalization, Sun Wukong is no longer a single, fixed cultural symbol but a multiple image that integrates different cultural elements. This cross-cultural integration makes the image of Sun Wukong more three-dimensional and diversified.

The financial transformation of enterprises from the perspective of business and finance integration
Abstract
Under the background of “Internet Plus” and big data, the transformation from traditional accounting finance to new management finance has become an inevitable trend. At present, the domestic economic development is slowing down, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises, whose survival space is getting narrower and narrower, and their development is facing numerous difficulties. In this situation, how to leverage the value creation capacity of finance to enhance enterprise efficiency, help enterprises get out of difficulties and achieve value appreciation is of practical significance. This article takes SMIC Holdings Limited as an example to study the financial transformation of the manufacturing industry from the perspective of business and finance integration. Firstly, the current financial situation of SMIC was analyzed, and it was found that there were problems such as a sound organizational structure but low management efficiency, traditional accounting supervision failing to create value, and the role of informatization not being fully exerted. Then, it elaborated in detail on the path of SMIC's implementation of business and finance integration and financial transformation, including organizational structure adjustment, establishment of system data interfaces and system architecture, and full implementation of information management, etc. Through the integration of business and finance, SMIC has achieved the optimization of fund management, the auxiliary application of comprehensive budget management, and the strengthening of asset management. Finally, the financial performance of SMIC after its transformation was evaluated through the financial indicator analysis method. It was found that its short-term debt-paying ability and operational capacity had significantly improved, and its profitability remained stable and showed an upward trend despite the downward pressure in the industry.

Abstract
Driven by the deep integration of “Internet+” and big data technologies, traditional financial management models are evolving into modern, management-oriented financial systems centered on the integration of business and finance. Against the backdrop of slowing macroeconomic growth and intensifying industry competition, enterprises urgently need to transform their financial functions to enhance operational efficiency and decision-making quality, thereby achieving sustainable development. This study selects SMIC, a globally leading integrated circuit manufacturing enterprise, as a typical case. From the perspective of "business-finance integration," it delves into the internal motivations, specific pathways, and implementation effectiveness of financial transformation for manufacturing enterprises in the digital wave.The research finds that prior to its transformation, despite having a relatively sound organizational structure, SMIC faced challenges such as suboptimal management efficiency, traditional accounting and supervision failing to effectively support value creation, and underutilized potential of its information systems. To address these challenges, the company systematically implemented a transformation path centered on organizational structure optimization, data platform construction, and business process reengineering. Specific measures included establishing dedicated positions for business-finance integration, achieving one-way data flow between business and finance systems by building interfaces, and promoting informatized management in key processes such as procurement, sales, and comprehensive budgeting through a project-based approach.

Abstract
As the ESG concept deepens globally, ESG performance has gradually become a crucial indicator for measuring a company's sustainable development capabilities and exerts profound impacts on external regulation and risk assessment. This paper uses Chinese A-share listed companies from 2019 to 2023, excluding ST and financial sectors (as defined by the CSRC in 2012), as a sample to empirically examine the mechanism and economic consequences of corporate ESG performance on audit fees. The study finds that good ESG performance can significantly reduce audit costs. Mechanism tests show that ESG performance enhances information quality, alleviating information asymmetry, which in turn reduces audit risks and workload, ultimately decreasing audit fees. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that compared to state-owned enterprises, non-state-owned enterprises exhibit a more pronounced inhibitory effect of ESG performance on audit fees. The findings provide empirical support for listed companies to optimize their ESG practices, audit firms to integrate ESG evaluation tools, and regulatory authorities to improve ESG policy frameworks, further expanding the research boundaries of ESG economic consequences and audit pricing theory.
Key words: ESG performance; audit fee; information disclosure quality

4.2 Consideration of Vocabulary Selection
In exploring the specific aspects of word choice in depth, we will first focus on words with emotional overtones. These words play an important role in language expression, because they can convey the speaker or author's emotional attitude, make the language more vivid and touching. However, in addition to emotional color, there is another key factor to consider in word selection, and that is figurative words. Figurative words are like artistic treasures within language. They create rich images and deep meanings by comparing one thing to another with similar characteristics. The use of this kind of vocabulary can not only enhance the expression of language, but also stimulate the imagination of readers, make abstract concepts concrete, and simplify complex emotions.
4.2.1 Vocabulary with Emotional Color
Vocabulary with emotional color refers to words that have the ability to evoke specific emotions or feelings in the reader. In the realm of cosmetics instructions, the use of such vocabulary can significantly boost the text’s persuasiveness and create a more engaging reading experience. For instance, a Chinese cosmetics instruction may use words like “luxurious,” “pampering,” or “indulgent” to describe a product, painting a picture of a lavish and indulgent experience for the user.
When translating this text into English, the translator must carefully select vocabulary with similar emotional connotations. Using words like “luxurious,” “pampering,” or “indulgent” in the English version preserves the aesthetic appeal of the original text and creates a similar emotional impact on the English reader. This not only maintains the intended tone and mood of the original but also makes the product more appealing and desirable to the target audience.Moreover, the use of vocabulary with emotional color can help establish a stronger connection between the brand and the consumer. By using words that evoke positive emotions, the translator can create a sense of familiarity and trust, making the consumer more likely to invest in the product. This emotional connection is crucial in the cosmetics industry, where consumers often seek products that not only meet their physical needs but also provide a sense of emotional satisfaction.
4.2.2 Figurative Vocabulary
Figurative vocabulary refers to words that create vivid imagery or use figurative language, such as similes, metaphors, or idioms. In cosmetics instructions, the use of figurative vocabulary can greatly enhance the text’s aesthetic appeal by creating a more engaging and visually appealing reading experience.
A Chinese cosmetics instruction may use figurative language to describe a product’s effectiveness, such as “erases fine lines like a magic eraser.” This phrase creates a vivid image in the reader’s mind, making the product’s effectiveness seem more tangible and appealing. When translating this text into English, the translator should strive to retain the figurative language by using a similar phrase, such as “erases fine lines like a magic eraser.” This preserves the aesthetic effect of the original text and creates a similar visual and emotional impact on the English reader.By using figurative vocabulary, the translator can also add depth and richness to the translated text. Similes, metaphors, and idioms can help convey complex ideas and emotions in a concise and memorable way. They can make the text more expressive and vivid, allowing the reader to form a clearer mental image of the product and its benefits.
Furthermore, the use of figurative vocabulary can contribute to the overall branding and marketing strategy of the cosmetics product. By creating vivid and memorable imagery, the translator can help the product stand out in a crowded market and leave a lasting impression on the consumer. This can ultimately lead to increased brand recognition and customer loyalty.
In conclusion, the consideration of vocabulary selection is crucial in the translation of cosmetics instructions. By carefully selecting vocabulary with emotional color and figurative vocabulary, the translator can preserve the aesthetic appeal of the original text and create a similar emotional and visual impact on the target audience. This not only enhances the persuasiveness and effectiveness of the translated text but also contributes to the overall success of the cosmetics product in the market.

This study has examined the translation of cosmetics instructions from Chinese to English, focusing on the application of translation aesthetic theory. The analysis has covered the use of rhetorical devices, consideration of vocabulary selection, and the overall aesthetic appeal of the translated text.
5.1 Major Findings
This research has delved into the translation of cosmetic instructions from a Translation Aesthetics perspective, with the primary objective of exploring how to effectively convey linguistic beauty, formal beauty, and cultural beauty in the translation process. By employing a literature review method to comb through the Translation Aesthetics theory and conducting case studies and comparative analyses of cosmetic instruction translation examples, this study has comprehensively examined the application of Translation Aesthetics in cosmetic instruction translation, covering aesthetic features and translation strategies at the lexical, syntactic, and textual levels.
The findings of this research indicate that the combination of literal translation and free translation, among other strategies, can effectively transmit aesthetic elements and enhance the quality of translation in cosmetic instructions. This approach allows for the preservation of the original text’s intent and imagery while adapting the language to suit the target audience’s cultural and linguistic preferences. By considering both the surface meanings and deeper aesthetic implications of the source text, translators can create translations that are not only accurate but also engaging and visually appealing.
At the lexical level, this study has highlighted the importance of selecting appropriate words and phrases that not only convey the intended meaning but also resonate with the aesthetic sensibilities of the target language. This involves considering factors such as connotations, collocations, and the overall tone and style of the text. For instance, using vivid and evocative language can help create a more immersive and engaging experience for the reader, thereby enhancing the aesthetic appeal of the translation.
At the syntactic level, this research has emphasized the need for translators to be mindful of the syntactic structures and patterns that contribute to the aesthetic qualities of the source text. This may involve reproducing certain syntactic features in the target text or adapting them to better suit the target language while still preserving the original’s aesthetic intent. For example, maintaining a consistent sentence structure or rhythm can contribute to the overall aesthetic effect of the translation.
At the textual level, this study has underscored the significance of considering the text’s overall structure, coherence, and cohesion in translation. This includes paying attention to the organization of information, the use of rhetorical devices, and the overall flow and pacing of the text. By reproducing these textual features in the target language, translators can create translations that are not only informative but also aesthetically pleasing and engaging to read.
Furthermore, this research has demonstrated the value of incorporating cultural considerations into the translation process. Cosmetic instructions, like any other marketing materials, are deeply embedded in cultural contexts and often contain cultural references and connotations. By being aware of these cultural nuances and adapting the translation accordingly, translators can ensure that the aesthetic qualities of the source text are effectively conveyed to the target audience.
One of the key innovations of this research lies in its application of Translation Aesthetics theory to the field of cosmetic instruction translation. This approach has enriched the existing research in this area by providing a theoretical framework for analyzing and evaluating the aesthetic qualities of translations. By focusing on the aesthetic aspects of translation, this research has contributed to a more nuanced and comprehensive understanding of the translation process and its outcomes.
The significance of this research is twofold: theoretical and practical. At the theoretical level, this study has expanded the scope of Translation Aesthetics theory by applying it to a specific and previously unexplored domain – cosmetic instruction translation. This contribution enhances the theory’s explanatory power and versatility, demonstrating its applicability to various types of texts and translation contexts.
At the practical level, this research provides valuable guidance for translators working on cosmetic instructions. By offering a set of translation strategies and principles based on Translation Aesthetics theory, this study equips translators with the tools and knowledge necessary to create translations that are both accurate and aesthetically appealing. This, in turn, can enhance the effectiveness of cosmetic instructions as marketing materials and contribute to the success of cosmetic products in international markets.
In conclusion, this research has made a significant contribution to the field of translation studies by exploring the application of Translation Aesthetics theory to cosmetic instruction translation. By focusing on the aesthetic qualities of translations and providing practical strategies for achieving these qualities, this study has not only enriched the theoretical understanding of translation but also offered valuable insights for translators working in the cosmetic industry. As such, this research has the potential to impact both the theory and practice of translation, ultimately contributing to the advancement of the field.
5.2 Limitations and Implications
While this study has provided valuable insights into the translation of cosmetics instructions from Chinese to English, there are some limitations that should be noted. First, the analysis was conducted on a limited sample of cosmetics instructions, which may not be representative of the entire field. Future research could expand the sample size to include a wider range of cosmetics instructions and product types.
Second, the study focused primarily on the aesthetic aspects of translation, without considering other important factors such as product-specific terminology or cultural differences in beauty standards. Future research could explore the interplay between aesthetic considerations and other factors in the translation of cosmetics instructions.
In conclusion, this study has highlighted the importance of translation aesthetic theory in the translation of cosmetics instructions from Chinese to English. By considering the use of rhetorical devices, vocabulary selection, and overall aesthetic appeal, translators can create translated texts that effectively communicate the product’s benefits and usage instructions to the target audience, while also preserving the aesthetic qualities of the original text.

4.3.3 Overall Considerations and Aesthetic Presentations at the Textual Level
4.3.3.1 Style and Logic Unity
Maintaining and Enhancing the Overall Style
	The overall style of the translation is consistent with that of the original text, both focusing on accurately and vividly describing the product's efficacy and makeup look. Through the use of aesthetically appealing words such as "innovative", "natural", "matte", and smooth sentence structures, a professional and fashionable atmosphere is created, which conforms to the product image of cosmetics, achieving style unity and an enhanced aesthetic effect at the textual level.
Enhancement of Logical Coherence
	In the text, conjunctions and logical relation words such as "and", "for", "even" are reasonably used to closely connect the different efficacies and makeup look characteristics of the product. For example, when describing the usage effects of different skin types, "for" is used to introduce different situations, making the comparison clearer. "And" is used to connect effects like oil control and no dryness or peeling, strengthening the expression of the parallel relationship. "Even" highlights the characteristic that the makeup will not look heavy even with multiple layers of application, further strengthening the product's advantages. The application of these conjunctions makes the text logic more coherent, enabling readers to easily understand the product's performance in various situations and the interrelationships among various characteristics, so as to better grasp the overall features of the product.
In conclusion, through the case analysis of the C-E translations of the instructions for the three cosmetics brands, namely Florasis, Carslan, and Maogeping, it can be seen that in the translation process, translators, based on the translation aesthetic theory, skillfully handle culturally-loaded words, accurately translate descriptive words, reasonably adjust syntactic structures, and pay attention to the overall style and logical coherence at the textual level, successfully realizing the organic combination of linguistic beauty, formal beauty, and cultural beauty. This not only enables the translation to accurately convey product information but also shows the aesthetic charm of cosmetics, effectively promoting the cross-cultural communication and promotion of cosmetics in the international market, providing useful references and examples for the translation of cosmetics instructions. Meanwhile, it also indicates that the translation aesthetic theory has important guiding significance in the translation practice of cosmetics instructions, helping to improve the translation quality and meet the cognitive and aesthetic needs of consumers in the target market.
Chapter 5 Conclusion
This study has conducted an in-depth exploration of the Chinese-English translation of cosmetics instructions from the perspective of translation aesthetics. Through a literature review to sort out the translation aesthetics theory and a detailed analysis of the translation examples of cosmetics instructions, it has systematically examined the application of translation aesthetics in the translation of cosmetics instructions, covering the aesthetic characteristics and corresponding translation strategies at the lexical, syntactic, and discourse levels.
The research results show that strategies such as the combination of literal translation and free translation can effectively transmit aesthetic elements and improve the translation quality of cosmetics instructions. In the process of translation, the translator, by taking into account both the surface meaning and the deeper aesthetic connotations of the source text, has successfully created translations that are not only accurate but also attractive and visually appealing. For example, in the translation of brand names and special ingredient names, "花西子" is translated as "Florasis", cleverly retaining the cultural charm of the brand; in the translation of descriptive words, "细腻粉质" is translated as "exquisite and fine - grained powder", accurately presenting the texture of the powder from different angles. At the syntactic level, optimizing the sentence structure makes the translation more compact and logical, as seen in the adjustment of the sentence structure in the translation of the Carslan liquid foundation instruction. At the discourse level, maintaining and enhancing the overall style and using conjunctions rationally improve the logical coherence, such as the use of conjunctions in the translation of the Maogeping powder comp.
Although this study has provided valuable insights into the Chinese-English translation of cosmetics instructions, it still has certain limitations. First, the sample of cosmetics instructions on which the analysis is based is limited and may not fully represent the diversity of the entire field of cosmetics instructions. Future research could further expand the sample size to cover more types, styles, and functions of cosmetics instructions to enhance the representativeness of the research results.
Secondly, this study mainly focuses on the aesthetic aspects of translation and does not fully consider other important factors such as product-specific terminology or cultural differences in beauty standards. In actual translation, these factors may have an important impact on the translation effect. Future research could explore in depth the interaction between aesthetic considerations and these factors in the translation of cosmetics instructions to gain a more comprehensive understanding of the complexity of cosmetics instructions translation.
In conclusion, this study highlights the importance of translation aesthetics theory in the Chinese-English translation of cosmetics instructions. Translators, by comprehensively considering the use of rhetorical devices, vocabulary selection, and overall aesthetic appeal, can create translations that effectively convey the product's benefits and usage instructions while retaining the aesthetic qualities of the original text. This not only helps to promote the cross-cultural communication and promotion of cosmetics in the international market but also provides useful references for translation practice and research in related fields, promoting the continuous improvement of the translation quality of cosmetics instructions and better meeting the cognitive and aesthetic needs of consumers in the target market.

Conclusion
Patients with cervical spinal cord injury (SCI) face severe respiratory dysfunction, which can lead to respiratory failure and other serious complications. Various methods have been employed to improve respiratory function and enhance the quality of life for these patients. Among these methods, diaphragmatic muscle training has been proven to be an effective approach in improving lung function and respiratory capacity.
Diaphragmatic muscle training strengthens respiratory muscles, especially the diaphragm, thereby increasing lung capacity and respiratory efficiency. In SCI patients, this training has a significant impact on alleviating breathing difficulties, increasing lung volume, and improving lung capacity. Through diaphragmatic muscle training, patients can enhance lung capacity, improve breathing depth, enhance gas exchange efficiency, reduce the risk of pulmonary infections, and enhance overall quality of life.
Furthermore, diaphragmatic muscle training can assist patients in the weaning process from ventilators, expediting the rehabilitation process. It enhances patients' respiratory tolerance, reduces dependence on ventilators, and promotes the recovery of respiratory function. For SCI patients who require long-term ventilator support, the application of diaphragmatic muscle training may signify a better quality of life and a faster recovery process.
In summary, diaphragmatic muscle training plays a positive role in the rehabilitation process of patients with cervical spinal cord injuries. 礼貌原则
On conversational implicature in Thunderstorm from the perspective of cooperative principle and politeness principle
Abstract
Thunderstorm is a renowned play in modern Chinese drama, written by Cao Yu in 1933. The play explores the complex emotional struggles, family conflicts, and societal tensions within early 20th-century Chinese society. This research aims to analyze the conversational implicature in Thunderstorm through the theoretical frameworks of the Cooperative Principle and the Politeness Principle. By examining the violations of these principles in the characters' dialogues, the study reveals the hidden emotional states, social conflicts, and power dynamics that shape the play's narrative and character development. The analysis of indirect speech, evasions, and omissions highlights the psychological complexity of the characters, such as Zhou Pu Yuan's manipulations and Zhou Fanyi's emotional struggles. The study further shows how these implicatures contribute to the advancement of the plot, escalation of conflicts, and enhancement of dramatic tension. This paper not only provides a deeper understanding of the play's language but also offers insights into the role of conversational implicature in reflecting social culture and power structures. Ultimately, this research underscores the significance of pragmatic analysis in literary criticism.
Key words: conversational implicature; Cooperative Principle; Politeness Principle
Chapter 1 Introduction
1.1 Research Background
Thunderstorm is one of the classic plays in modern Chinese literature, through which Cao Yu deeply explores the class conflicts, family disputes, and emotional struggles within early 20th-century Chinese society. In the play, the characters' dialogues not only drive the plot forward but also reveal the inner world of the characters and their complex social relationships through implicit meanings. Every conversation is filled with linguistic hints, and the words of the characters often conceal deep emotions and conflicts beneath the surface.
From a pragmatics perspective, the Cooperative Principle and the Politeness Principle provide an effective theoretical framework for analyzing these implicit meanings. The Cooperative Principle, proposed by Grice, emphasizes that communicators should provide appropriate information based on the communication goals, ensuring that the dialogue flows smoothly and effectively. The four maxims of the Cooperative Principle—Quantity, Quality, Relation, and Manner—constitute the basic linguistic norms of interpersonal communication. Communicators usually follow or intentionally violate these maxims based on their communicative goals to convey more implicit meanings. The Politeness Principle, on the other hand, focuses on how language helps maintain interpersonal relationships, avoid conflicts, and ensure appropriateness in communication. Its six maxims, such as Tact, Generosity, and Approbation, reflect the social and cultural aspects of the communicators' linguistic behavior.
